title: The cortico-basal ganglia–thalamic network: a connectomic framework
title_zh: 皮层-基底神经节-丘脑网络：连接组学框架
abstract: Classical anatomical and physiological studies have established the cortico-basal ganglia–thalamic (CBGT) system as a set of topographically organized, functionally specialized circuits that link the cerebral cortex, basal ganglia and thalamus while allowing convergence and interaction between information streams. Recent advances in mesoscale and single-neuron connectomics now enable these organizational principles to be resolved at unprecedented spatial and cellular scales. Here we synthesize the findings of recent connectomic studies of the CBGT network to define an emerging structural and network framework. Modern connectomic data reveal how parallel processing and information integration are implemented through a multiscale architecture characterized by modular organization, graded and overlapping boundaries, stage-specific patterns of segregation and convergence, and re-entrant interactions among cortical, basal ganglia, thalamic and brainstem nodes. Molecular, transcriptomic and neuronal morphological datasets further reveal spatial heterogeneity that broadly aligns with this connectivity-defined organization. This structural framework provides a foundation for understanding how CBGT networks preserve functional specialization while enabling cross-domain integration and generates testable hypotheses about the links between circuit architecture and neural computation, behaviour and dysfunction in neurological and psychiatric disorders. The cortico-basal ganglia–thalamic (CBGT) system supports a wide range of behaviours through its modular network organization. Dong and colleagues describe how advanced mesoscale and single-neuron connectomics has refined our understanding of CBGT circuit architecture, providing insights into the network’s capacity to preserve functional specialization while integrating across sensory, motor and cognitive domains.
abstract_zh: 经典的解剖和生理学研究已将皮层-基底神经节-丘脑（CBGT）系统确立为一组按空间组织、功能专用的电路，这些电路连接大脑皮层、基底神经节和丘脑，并允许信息流之间的汇聚与相互作用。近年来，在中尺度和单细胞连接组学方面的进步，现在使得以前所未有的空间和细胞分辨率解析这些组织原理成为可能。本文综合了CBGT网络近期连接组学研究的发现，定义了一个新兴的结构和网络框架。现代连接组学数据揭示了如何通过多尺度架构实现并行处理和信息整合，其特征是模块化组织、渐进且重叠的边界、特定阶段的分离与汇聚模式，以及皮层、基底神经节、丘脑和脑干节点之间的再入相互作用。分子、转录组和神经元形态学数据进一步揭示了与这种连接定义的组织广泛一致的空间异质性。这一结构框架为理解CBGT网络如何在保持功能专用的同时实现跨域整合提供了基础，并针对电路结构与神经计算、行为以及神经精神病学障碍之间的联系产生了可检验的假设。CBGT系统通过其模块化网络组织支持广泛的行为。Dong及其同事描述了先进的中尺度和单细胞连接组学如何完善了我们对CBGT电路架构的理解，提供了关于网络在感觉、运动和认知域中保持功能专用同时整合能力的见解。
